question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s consolidated authority within the Communist Party, reinforced by the 2025 Fourth Plenum and ongoing elite purges, underpins traders’ strong expectation that he will remain in power through the end of 2026. With no designated successor and institutional norms around age limits largely set aside, analysts across reports view his fourth term at the 2027 Party Congress as the baseline outcome. Recent public messaging on economic planning and national security further signals continuity rather than transition. While the 95.8% implied probability for “No” reflects this broad consensus, low-probability shifts could still arise from sudden health developments, abrupt factional realignments, or an unforeseen crisis eroding elite support before year-end.

question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democratic Party sources.

Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains highly fluid this far from the primaries, with no formal declarations and trader consensus reflecting fragmented support across multiple figures. Gavin Newsom holds a narrow lead at 18.4% after earlier slippage from higher levels, while Jon Ossoff and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez sit just behind at 14.6% and 14.3%, respectively, amid rising visibility for Senate and House voices. Kamala Harris trails at 8.6% as the field weighs paths involving governors, senators, and other elected officials. Recent party discussions on the primary calendar and broader debates over positioning have kept probabilities tight, with separation likely hinging on future polling trends, endorsements, or early positioning moves before the 2028 cycle intensifies.
